contract: cramer3(a00,a01,a02, a10,a11,a12, a20,a21,a22, b0,b1,b2) -> [x0,x1,x2] | null. A is ROW-MAJOR. null when |det| < 1e-14.
expectations_from: Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting over exact rationals (Python fractions) — DELIBERATELY not Cramer rule, since expectations computed the same way the block computes would agree by construction and the table could not fail.

cases.name: textbook_integer
cases.why: A solution known independently of this repo; catches an index or sign transposition.

cases.name: identity
cases.why: Row-major argument order: a wrong order still passes on a symmetric matrix, not on this.

cases.name: bristorian_newton_step
cases.why: The actual call: Jacobian of Bristorian squaring at w=(1/4,1/2,1/8) with the negated residual. Dyadic on purpose — every entry exact in binary, so any error is arithmetic.

cases.name: singular_repeated_row
cases.why: det exactly 0 — a critical point of the squaring map in the real callers. Must be null.

cases.name: caveat_small_scale_rejected
cases.documents: THE TOLERANCE IS ABSOLUTE. This system is the identity scaled by 1e-5 — condition number 1, exactly solvable, answer [1,2,3]. |det| is 1e-15, under the 1e-14 floor, so it is REJECTED. A caller working at small scale loses well-conditioned systems.
cases.why: The first half of the block known caveat, made executable.

cases.name: caveat_large_scale_accepted
cases.documents: THE OTHER HALF. Rows 1 and 2 differ by 1e-12 in one slot and the whole matrix is scaled by 1e5, so |det| is 3000 — comfortably accepted — while the answer carries 2e-3 relative error. Accepted, and wrong in the third digit.
cases.why: Needed two attempts to build: the first version put the rhs where the near-dependency cancels and the solve came back exact to 1e-16, which would have documented a caveat that does not bite. The rhs must not lie in the well-conditioned direction.
